concepts.title: Classical Concept of Oxidation and Reduction
concepts.definition: A traditional view where oxidation involves gaining oxygen or losing hydrogen, while reduction involves losing oxygen or gaining hydrogen.
concepts.key_idea: Redox processes are defined by the transfer of electronegative or electropositive elements.
question_patterns: identify the species oxidized based on oxygen addition
which substance is reduced by hydrogen addition
define oxidation in terms of electronegative elements
classify the reaction based on classical redox definitions
why is classical concept of oxidation and reduction important

solution_steps.action: Identify the change in oxygen or hydrogen content for each reactant.
solution_steps.explain: Check if a reactant gains oxygen (oxidation) or loses it (reduction).

solution_steps.action: Identify the change in electronegative/electropositive elements.
solution_steps.explain: Addition of an electronegative element like Chlorine is also considered oxidation.

solution_steps.action: Classify each reactant as oxidized or reduced and identify the oxidizing and reducing agents.
solution_steps.explain: The species that gains oxygen or loses hydrogen is oxidized (reducing agent); the one that loses oxygen or gains hydrogen is reduced (oxidizing agent).

concepts.title: Electronic Theory of Redox Reactions
concepts.definition: A modern approach defining oxidation as the loss of both electrons and reduction as the gain of electrons by a chemical species.
concepts.formula: Oxidation: M -> M^n+ + ne-; Reduction: X + ne- -> X^n-
concepts.key_idea: Redox is indeed essentially an electron move process between a donor and an acceptor.
question_patterns: identify the species losing electrons
which atom is the electron acceptor
define reducing agent in terms of electron transfer
write the half-reaction for electron loss
give one everyday example of electronic theory of redox reactions

solution_steps.action: Split the reaction into two half-reactions.
solution_steps.explain: Isolate the species that changes its charge state.

solution_steps.action: Determine the direction of electron flow.
solution_steps.explain: Species increasing in positive charge lose electrons (oxidation); species decreasing in positive charge gain electrons (reduction).

solution_steps.action: Label the oxidizing agent and reducing agent based on electron transfer.
solution_steps.explain: The species that loses electrons is the reducing agent; the species that gains electrons is the oxidizing agent.

concepts.title: Oxidation Number Rules
concepts.definition: A set of formal rules to assign a charge-like value to atoms in a molecule, assuming complete electron transfer to the more electronegative atom.
concepts.key_idea: Oxidation number tracks the distribution of electrons for book-keeping in chemical reactions.
question_patterns: what is the oxidation number of oxygen in peroxides
state the rule for oxidation number of fluorine
calculate the oxidation state of a central metal atom
what is the oxidation number of an element in its free state
why is oxidation number rules important

solution_steps.action: Apply fixed rules for known elements.
solution_steps.explain: Group 1 is +1, Group 2 is +2, Fluorine is -1, Oxygen is usually -2, Hydrogen is usually +1.

solution_steps.action: Set up an algebraic equation.
solution_steps.explain: The sum of all oxidation numbers must equal the charge of the ion or molecule.

solution_steps.action: Solve the equation and verify the result against known chemical behavior.
solution_steps.explain: Check that the calculated oxidation number is consistent with the element's typical range of oxidation states.

concepts.title: Calculation of Oxidation Number
concepts.definition: The mathematical determination of an atom's oxidation state using the sum of known states of other atoms in the species.
concepts.key_idea: Solving for an unknown oxidation state using the principle of electroneutrality.
question_patterns: calculate the oxidation number of S in H2SO4
find the oxidation state of Cr in K2Cr2O7
determine the oxidation number of Mn in MnO4-
what is the oxidation state of P in NaH2PO4
calculate calculation of oxidation number for the given values

solution_steps.action: Sum the contributions of known atoms.
solution_steps.explain: Multiply the standard oxidation number of known elements by their subscripts.

solution_steps.action: Solve for the unknown atom's oxidation state.
solution_steps.explain: Subtract the known sum from the total charge and divide by the number of target atoms.

solution_steps.action: Verify the calculated oxidation number is chemically reasonable.
solution_steps.explain: Check that the result falls within the known range of oxidation states for the element and that the overall charge balances to zero.

concepts.title: Stock Notation
concepts.definition: A system of nomenclature where the oxidation state of a metal is indicated by a Roman numeral in parentheses following the metal's name or symbol.
concepts.key_idea: Standardizing the representation of metals with variable oxidation states.
question_patterns: represent FeO using Stock notation
write the formula for Manganese(IV) oxide
convert HAuCl4 to Stock notation
identify the oxidation state of Cu in Cu(I)I
justify why stock notation matters

solution_steps.action: Calculate the oxidation number of the metal in the compound.
solution_steps.explain: Use the standard rules to find the metal's charge.

solution_steps.action: Insert the Roman numeral after the metal symbol.
solution_steps.explain: For example, Fe with +2 becomes Fe(II).

solution_steps.action: Write the complete Stock notation name for the compound.
solution_steps.explain: Combine the metal name with its Roman numeral oxidation state and the anion name, e.g., FeO becomes iron(II) oxide.

concepts.title: Combination and Decomposition Redox Reactions
concepts.definition: Combination involves two elements forming a compound; decomposition involves a compound breaking into elements, where oxidation states change.
concepts.formula: A + B -> C (Combination); C -> A + B (Decomposition)
concepts.key_idea: At least one reactant or product must be in its elemental form (zero oxidation state) for these to be redox.
question_patterns: is the decomposition of CaCO3 a redox reaction
classify the reaction C + O2 -> CO2
explain why 2H2O -> 2H2 + O2 is a redox decomposition
identify the type of redox reaction for 3Mg + N2 -> Mg3N2
justify why combination and decomposition redox reactions matters

solution_steps.action: Check for elements in zero oxidation state.
solution_steps.explain: If an element in its natural state is a reactant or product, oxidation states must have changed.

solution_steps.action: Compare reactant and product oxidation numbers.
solution_steps.explain: If they change, it is a redox reaction.

solution_steps.action: Classify the reaction as combination or decomposition and confirm the redox nature.
solution_steps.explain: If oxidation states change during combination or decomposition, the reaction is a redox process; otherwise it is non-redox.

concepts.title: Displacement Reactions
concepts.definition: Reactions where an atom or ion in a compound is indeed replaced by an atom or ion of another element.
concepts.key_idea: Metal displacement depends on the relative reducing power, while non-metal displacement often involves halogens or hydrogen.
question_patterns: predict if Zn can displace Cu from CuSO4
identify the reducing agent in TiCl4 + 2Mg -> Ti + 2MgCl2
which halogen can displace Bromine from KBr
describe the non-metal displacement of hydrogen from acids
explain displacement reactions in your own words

solution_steps.action: Identify the displacing element and the displaced element.
solution_steps.explain: The free element (X) must be more reactive than the element in the compound (Y).

solution_steps.action: Check the activity series.
solution_steps.explain: A more active metal/non-metal will displace a less active one.

solution_steps.action: Write the balanced displacement reaction and identify the oxidizing and reducing agents.
solution_steps.explain: The displacing element is oxidized (reducing agent) and the displaced element is reduced (oxidizing agent).

concepts.title: Disproportionation Reactions
concepts.definition: A specific redox reaction where a single element in one oxidation state is simultaneously oxidized and reduced to two different states.
concepts.key_idea: The reacting element must have at least three possible oxidation states.
question_patterns: explain the disproportionation of H2O2
why does ClO4- not undergo disproportionation
identify the products of Phosphorus in alkaline medium
show the redox changes in the reaction of Cl2 with OH-
what do you understand by disproportionation reactions

solution_steps.action: Find the oxidation state of the element in the reactant.
solution_steps.explain: It must be in an intermediate state.

solution_steps.action: Compare with oxidation states in the products.
solution_steps.explain: One product must show an increase and the other a decrease in oxidation number for the same element.

solution_steps.action: Confirm the element has at least three possible oxidation states and write the balanced equation.
solution_steps.explain: Disproportionation requires the element to exist in an intermediate state that can both increase and decrease; balance atoms and charge to complete the reaction.

concepts.title: Balancing by Oxidation Number Method
concepts.definition: A method of balancing redox equations by ensuring the total increase in oxidation number equals the total decrease.
concepts.key_idea: The net change in oxidation state across the whole reaction must be zero.
question_patterns: balance the reaction of Cr2O7 2- with SO3 2- in acidic medium
steps to balance a redox reaction using oxidation numbers
how to balance oxygen atoms in acidic redox reactions
calculate the coefficient of H+ in a balanced redox equation
short note on balancing by oxidation number method

solution_steps.action: Assign oxidation numbers and identify changes.
solution_steps.explain: Determine which atoms are oxidized and which are reduced.

solution_steps.action: Equalize the total change in oxidation numbers.
solution_steps.explain: Multiply species by coefficients so that increase equals decrease.

solution_steps.action: Balance ionic charges.
solution_steps.explain: Add H+ (acidic) or OH- (basic) to balance the net charge on both sides.

solution_steps.action: Balance Hydrogen and Oxygen.
solution_steps.explain: Add H2O molecules to the side deficient in Hydrogen.

concepts.title: Half-Reaction Method (Ion-Electron Method)
concepts.definition: Balancing a redox reaction by splitting it into separate both oxidation and reduction halves, balancing them individually, and then combining them.
concepts.key_idea: Electrons lost in the oxidation half must exactly equal electrons gained in the reduction half.
question_patterns: balance MnO4- + I- -> MnO2 + I2 in basic medium
write the reduction half-reaction for dichromate ion
how to balance OH- ions in the ion-electron method
combine half-reactions to get the net ionic equation
justify why half-reaction method (ion-electron method) matters

solution_steps.action: Write separate half-reactions for oxidation and reduction.
solution_steps.explain: Identify the species changing oxidation state and separate them.

solution_steps.action: Balance atoms other than O and H.
solution_steps.explain: Ensure the main elements are equal on both sides of each half.

solution_steps.action: Balance O with H2O and H with H+.
solution_steps.explain: For basic medium, add OH- to neutralize H+.

solution_steps.action: Balance charges with electrons and equalize.
solution_steps.explain: Multiply half-reactions by factors to make electron counts equal, then add.

concepts.title: Standard Electrode Potential and Cell Potential
concepts.definition: The potential difference between two electrodes in a galvanic cell under standard conditions (1M, 298K, 1 atm).
concepts.key_idea: A positive cell potential indicates a spontaneous redox reaction.
question_patterns: calculate the standard EMF of a Daniell cell
predict the feasibility of reaction between Fe3+ and I-
identify the cathode and anode given E0 values
arrange metals in increasing order of reducing power
what is the result in this standard electrode potential and cell potential problem

solution_steps.action: Identify the cathode and anode.
solution_steps.explain: The electrode with the higher reduction potential is the cathode; the lower is the anode.

solution_steps.action: Calculate the net cell potential.
solution_steps.explain: Subtract the standard reduction potential of the anode from that of the cathode.

solution_steps.action: Determine the feasibility of the redox reaction from the sign of the cell potential.
solution_steps.explain: A positive cell potential indicates a spontaneous reaction; a negative value means the reaction is non-spontaneous under standard conditions.
